must_remember: Surface tension ($T$ or $\sigma$) is defined as force per unit length with dimensions $[ML^0T^{-2}]$ and units $\text{N m}^{-1}$.
Surface energy ($E$) is the potential energy per unit surface area, numerically and dimensionally equal to surface tension.
Excess pressure inside a spherical liquid drop is $P = \frac{2T}{R}$ (one free surface).
Excess pressure inside a spherical soap bubble is $P = \frac{4T}{R}$ (two free surfaces).
Liquid wetting glass (e.g., water) forms a concave meniscus with an acute angle of contact ($\theta < 90^\circ$) and shows capillary rise.
Liquid not wetting glass (e.g., mercury) forms a convex meniscus with an obtuse angle of contact ($\theta > 90^\circ$) and shows capillary depression.
Capillary rise height is given by Jurin's Law: $h = \frac{2T \cos\theta}{r \rho g}$.
Work done in blowing a soap bubble from radius $R_1$ to $R_2$ is $W = 8\pi T(R_2^2 - R_1^2)$ due to two free surfaces.
Work done in merging $n$ identical small drops into one big drop is $W = 4\pi R^2 T(n^{1/3} - 1)$.
Surface tension decreases with temperature according to the relation $T_t = T_0(1 - \alpha t)$.

glossary.meaning: The tensile force acting per unit length imaginarily drawn on a liquid surface, perpendicular to the line.
The extra potential energy stored in the molecules present in the surface layer per unit surface area.
A sphere centered on a liquid molecule with a radius equal to the molecular range, within which intermolecular attractive forces are effective.
The angle subtended by the tangent to the liquid surface at the point of contact with a solid surface, measured inside the liquid.
The pressure difference between the concave and convex sides of a curved liquid surface caused by surface tension.
The phenomenon of rise or fall of a liquid inside a narrow tube (capillary tube) immersed in it.
The physical law stating that the height of capillary rise is inversely proportional to the radius of the capillary tube and density of the liquid.
